documents.title: Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of AGM
INTIMATION FOR RESCHEDULING OF 60TH ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF THE COMPANY ON 26TH AUGUST 2026 (WEDNESDAY) AT 12:00 NOON (IST)

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported stellar operational and financial performance for Q4 and the full year FY2025-26, achieving highest-ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT and record production across multiple value-added products. The company maintained a comfortable debt-equity ratio of 0.18 and recommended a final dividend of INR 54 per share, taking the total dividend to INR 62 per share. Management highlighted that future capex will focus on the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project, retail outlet network expansion, and ongoing energy efficiency schemes. Despite external global uncertainties and volatility, management remains focused on safe, reliable operations and capital discipline. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd reported a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT for FY 2024-25, achieving 99.5% of its installed capacity, alongside lower fuel and loss levels and an upgraded S&P Global ESG score of 46.

demand_outlook.claim: The southern market for Motor Spirit (MS) experiences a shortfall where production is less than demand by close to 20 TMT per month.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

demand_outlook.claim: Southern market growth projections are aligned closely with national growth forecasts, with MS projected around 4% to 5% and HSD at 3%.
demand_outlook.quote: As far as others are concerned, we have seen the southern market to be mostly aligned to the national growth projection. Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: The company states that approvals are in place and project execution has started in full swing for the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: Management notes that the retail outlet endeavor involving 300 licenses has started and commissioning will be seen during FY 2026-27.
capex_expansion.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

capex_expansion.claim: Management outlines capital expenditure details of INR 1,600 crores for the LOBS project and INR 400 crores for retail outlets over 2 to 3 years, alongside INR 500 crores in normal annual capex.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores. So that makes it INR2,000 crores. This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years. Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

capex_expansion.claim: In the current financial year, the company spent Rs. 673 crores as capital expenditure.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: The maintenance CAPEX is forecasted to remain in the Rs. 200-250 crore range, though actuals may vary depending on value-added project approvals.
capex_expansion.quote: Our maintenance CAPEX remains Rs. 200-250 crore range, and the next year forecast also, we feel the CAPEX will be in that range. The maintenance CAPEX will be at around Rs. 200-250 crore range and depending on value added projects approvals, the actual will be a little different.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the Cauvery Basin Refinery project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CBR update, in the last year we revised the capital cost as well as the capital structure. The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: The new refinery project has a capacity of 9 million metric tons with a petrochemical intensity of 6% for polypropylene.
capex_expansion.quote: The new refinery capital cost is Rs 36,000 Crore approximately, 9 million metric ton capacity and petrochemical intensity of 6% and which is PP, polypropylene.

margins_costs.claim: The gross refining margin for the fourth quarter was reported at $13.75 per barrel against the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: Management stated that the core GRM for the fourth quarter stood at $10.3 per barrel.
The Gross Refining Margin for the full year 2024-25 was $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: For the fourth quarter, the Gross Refining Margin was $6.22 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: On Quarter 4, our GRM was $6.22 per barrel.

margins_costs.claim: Inventory gain for the fourth quarter was $0.66 per barrel, amounting to Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: On an overall annual basis, the inventory registered a loss of $0.06 per barrel or Rs. 40 crores.
margins_costs.quote: But on an overall annual basis, the inventory would be a loss that is $ 0.06 per barrel, Rs. 40 crores in amount.

margins_costs.claim: Fuel and losses for the year came down to 8.51%.
margins_costs.quote: I must place it that if you remember our Energy Indexes and our Fuel and Loss Indexes were quite high 2-3 years back and we went to a roadmap where we said on a sustained basis, we will bring it down to very efficient levels and in that context, the fuel and loss has come down to 8.51% for the year as a whole.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a highest-ever annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, representing 112 percent of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: During the fourth quarter, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which equals 111 percent of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The company announced a capacity addition of 250 KTPA in Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS capacity through its new unit.
orders_capacity.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

capital_allocation.claim: The company's gross debt-equity ratio stands at 0.18 compared to 0.39 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: Our leverage position now stands at 0.18. Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: Gross borrowings stand at INR 1,900 crores, while net borrowings stand at INR 973 crores with a net debt ratio of 0.09.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores. If we consider net borrowing, the debt ratio is only 0.09, which is less than 0.1.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a final dividend of INR 54 per share, which, along with the interim dividend of INR 8, brings the total dividend for the year to INR 62 per share.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: The debt-to-equity position as of March 31, 2025, stands at 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: Total absolute debt as of March 31, 2025, is Rs. 3,100 crores compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as of March 31, 2024.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.

capital_allocation.claim: Net worth stood at Rs. 7,939 crores as of March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share, representing 50% of the face value for the current year.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management noted that uncertainties arising from logistical constraints and volatility in crude oil prices pose challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company reported a foreign exchange loss of approximately INR 200 crores for the quarter and around INR 350 crores for the full year.
risks_headwinds.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties arising from the volatility of crude prices pose a challenge to the business.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that the company is committed to developing new schemes focused on energy efficiency, fuel and loss reduction, and value-added product enhancement.
management_commitments.quote: CPCL is committed to develop new schemes on energy efficiency, further fuel and loss reduction and develop and enhancement value-added products.

management_commitments.claim: The company intends to further improve capacity utilization levels, energy intensity index, and fuel efficiency on a continuous basis.
management_commitments.quote: But yes, on the operational side, we intend to improve further on a capacity utilisation levels, on energy intensity index and fuel efficiency, we would improve on a continuous basis.

management_commitments.claim: Normal maintenance capital expenditure for the next two years is projected to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores per year.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
